description: Bounded optimization experiments. Legality is checked before profitability; no experiment result adopts a production rule.

provenance.jet_variant: Authored in each family fixture directory; no production optimizer or second compiler is introduced.
provenance.peer_variant: Matched Python implementation consumes the same declared input and expected output.
provenance.measurement: pending: no execution, timing, or adoption claim is authored in source
provenance.source_of_truth: Jet and peer fixture files plus raw checker/inspect/harness records

families.title: Checked arithmetic and Float rewrites
families.question: Can a checked integer or binary64 rewrite be selected without changing overflow, NaN, signed-zero, or evaluation-order observations?

machine_domain.integer: Jet Int is a target-described signed fixed-width two's-complement value; checked add traps before an unrepresentable result. The target width must be recorded before a result is usable.
machine_domain.float: IEEE-754 binary64, round-to-nearest-ties-to-even, with signed zero, NaN, infinity, and evaluation order observable; reassociation and fast-math are forbidden unless separately stated.
machine_domain.target: The report must bind the exact compiler target triple and floating-point lowering configuration; host defaults are not a proof.

premises: Every integer operation has a checked representability premise for the declared target width.
Float operands are finite only when the source record says so; no real-number associativity premise is inferred.
The source preserves operand evaluation order and typed failure order.
The candidate and control consume byte-identical input and emit the same target representation.

observations.result: Byte-exact numeric output, including signed-zero and NaN spelling where the runtime exposes it.
observations.typed_failure: Overflow and invalid-operation class, source identity, and lowest failing operation/index.
observations.mutation: No mutation may be introduced or removed around the arithmetic expression.
observations.input_consumption: Same operands, count, and consumption order; no skipped value after a checked failure.
observations.ordered_effects: Print/callback effects occur in source order and are not duplicated by speculative evaluation.
observations.cleanup: Any failure unwinds the same owned temporaries in the same order.
observations.resource_premises: Target width, floating-point mode, and checked-operation availability are recorded facts.
observations.allowed_schedules: Only schedules proved equivalent under the numeric contract are admitted; unrestricted reassociation is not admitted.
observations.identity: The inspected operation points to the same source span and compiler candidate identity as the raw record.

families.falsifier: Use the authored Float counterexample (1e16 + -1e16) + 1 versus 1e16 + (-1e16 + 1), and a target-width checked overflow boundary. Any changed bit, failure class, or effect order rejects the rewrite.

rule_record.candidate_rule: reassociate only under a checked machine-number contract
rule_record.decision: awaiting checker, same-job cost, and owner choice

families.title: Range and alias facts for fusion/vectorization
families.question: Can a range loop be fused or widened only when alias, bounds, lane order, and failure premises hold?

machine_domain.index: Finite half-open integer ranges with checked bounds; the exact input length is part of identity.
machine_domain.storage: Mutable contiguous list storage with explicit alias relation; a write window cannot overlap a read window unless the contract proves the overlap-safe order.
machine_domain.lanes: Integer lanes preserve element order and exact integer results; no masked lane may consume an element twice or hide a failure.
machine_domain.target: The report records vector width, alignment, bounds-check policy, and target representation before comparing cost.

premises: The range endpoints and stride are unchanged.
Read/write windows are disjoint or the transformation proves an overlap-safe direction.
The body has no observable effect or early failure that lane reordering would change.
Every bounds and alias fact is attached to the source identity.

observations.result: Byte-exact output list and reduction value for every element.
observations.typed_failure: Same bounds, alias, and body failure class at the same lowest index.
observations.mutation: Same cells are written once, in the same visible final state; no hidden temporary replaces an observed alias.
observations.input_consumption: Same range cardinality and read count; no speculative extra read beyond the source window.
observations.ordered_effects: Effects in the loop body retain source order; effectful bodies are not widened.
observations.cleanup: Temporary vector buffers and borrowed views release in the same order on success and failure.
observations.resource_premises: Alignment, lane width, allocation, and alias proofs are present and target-bound.
observations.schedule: Sequential index order is the control; candidate lane order is explicit.
observations.allowed_schedules: Only non-overlapping, order-equivalent lanes may be fused or vectorized.
observations.identity: Range, storage, and alias facts carry the source and input digests into the inspect record.

families.falsifier: Run the negative control with overlapping read/write windows and an effectful body. A changed element, duplicate read, changed lowest failure, or reordered print rejects fusion/vectorization.

rule_record.candidate_rule: fuse or widen only from explicit range and non-overlap facts
rule_record.decision: awaiting checker, same-job cost, and owner choice

families.title: Specialization and comptime staging
families.question: Can a stable compile-time fact specialize a hot path without stale reuse, effect loss, or loss of the runtime fallback?

machine_domain.stage: Comptime bindings are evaluated by the declared Jet staging evaluator and their source/environment digest is part of identity.
machine_domain.runtime: Runtime inputs remain typed Int values with checked operations; a dynamic value must use the fallback path when the specialization premise is absent.
machine_domain.effects: Only the declared pure/comptime effect set may execute during specialization; IO, time, environment, and mutation are not silently staged.
machine_domain.target: The report records compiler target, specialization configuration, code-size identity, and invalidation key.

premises: Specialized values are stable for the full job and have a matching source/environment digest.
All effects and typed failures are preserved at the same stage or explicitly rejected.
A runtime fallback exists for changed or unavailable inputs.
Invalidation occurs before a stale specialization is reused.

observations.result: Warm and cold executions produce the same byte-exact result for equal inputs.
observations.typed_failure: The same invalid input produces the same typed failure and location, whether specialized or fallback.
observations.mutation: Runtime state is not frozen into a stale compile-time value; state updates remain visible.
observations.input_consumption: Runtime inputs consumed by the fallback are not removed by specialization.
observations.ordered_effects: Effects remain at their declared stage and source order.
observations.cleanup: Staged temporaries and runtime resources have matching cleanup obligations.
observations.resource_premises: Code size, retained specialization state, invalidation key, and cache lifetime are recorded.
observations.schedule: Specialization changes representation only; it does not change an effectful schedule.
observations.allowed_schedules: Only stage-equivalent pure work may move to comptime; dynamic/effectful work stays runtime.
observations.identity: The specialization key joins source, input, compiler, target, and environment identities.

families.falsifier: Re-run the authored program after changing the specialization input from 4 to 5 without rebuilding the source identity. A stale 12, lost fallback, or shifted effect rejects the specialization.

rule_record.candidate_rule: specialize stable pure inputs and invalidate on identity change
rule_record.decision: awaiting checker, same-job cost, and owner choice

families.title: No-semantic-copy layout selection
families.question: Can a layout representation change avoid a semantic copy while preserving identity, fields, ownership, and foreign-visible offsets?

machine_domain.representation: The candidate uses the declared C-compatible field order and target alignment; offsets and stride are target facts, not inferred host constants.
machine_domain.identity: A record identity and field ownership remain observable even when storage is re-packed internally.
machine_domain.boundary: No external pointer, ABI consumer, raw address, or foreign callback may observe an unapproved layout change.
machine_domain.target: The report records target triple, ABI, alignment, field offsets, stride, and representation digest.

premises: No source or foreign consumer observes the old address or offset unless the declared layout contract preserves it.
All fields and ownership transitions are preserved exactly.
A copy is not removed when it is the required ownership boundary.
The selected representation is legal before cache or bandwidth cost is considered.

observations.result: The same field values and serialized output are observed by the Jet and peer programs.
observations.typed_failure: Field access, ownership, and foreign-boundary failures remain the same.
observations.mutation: Mutating one logical record changes the same owner and field, not a detached copy.
observations.input_consumption: The same records and fields are read once; no hidden materialization drops a field.
observations.ordered_effects: Foreign calls and visible writes retain source order.
observations.cleanup: The same owner releases fields and any temporary layout buffer in the same order.
observations.resource_premises: Copy bytes, cache-block memory, alignment, stride, and retention are recorded.
observations.schedule: Layout changes do not alter logical iteration order.
observations.allowed_schedules: Only internal layouts with an explicit no-observable-copy relation are allowed.
observations.identity: Layout facts, field offsets, target representation, and source identity join in the inspect record.

families.falsifier: Pass the layout to a consumer that reads the old field offset or mutate through an alias. A changed field, pointer identity, ownership release, or foreign-visible offset rejects no-semantic-copy.

rule_record.candidate_rule: remove only copies with a proven no-observable-copy relation
rule_record.decision: awaiting checker, same-job cost, and owner choice

families.title: Conditional parallel scheduling
families.question: Does a bounded parallel schedule preserve independent-kernel behavior and win only when measured work amortizes setup and bandwidth cost?

machine_domain.kernel: Finite independent Int iterations with no shared mutation, IO, callbacks, or early exit; each result is deterministic.
machine_domain.schedule: para_map preserves source order and uses a bounded worker limit; cancellation and lowest failing index are part of the contract.
machine_domain.gate: Automatic acceleration is eligible only above the 1024-item floor when projected gain is at least 2x spawn cost plus the bandwidth floor; first chunk timing is retained.
machine_domain.resources: Parallelism uses the existing pool and bounded per-cache-block memory; no new threads are created by the experiment.

premises: Every iteration is independent and has the same typed result and failure behavior.
The pool limit, chunk partition, and cancellation policy are recorded.
The candidate and control consume the same 1024-item input and output all required observations.
A cost win is reported per mode/tier and is not inferred from sampled or historical probes.

observations.result: Byte-exact ordered output and complete result count.
observations.typed_failure: Same lowest failing index, failure type, and sibling cancellation behavior.
observations.mutation: No shared mutable cell is written by independent iterations; output slots are disjoint.
observations.input_consumption: Each input is consumed exactly once and no work past cancellation is reported as completed.
observations.ordered_effects: Effectful callbacks are excluded unless their order is explicitly preserved.
observations.cleanup: Every worker, chunk, and resource is joined/released on success and failure.
observations.resource_premises: Pool size, spawn cost, cache-block bytes, bandwidth floor, and peak memory are recorded.
observations.schedule: Control is sequential; candidate records chunks, worker limit, first chunk timing, and completion order.
observations.allowed_schedules: Only bounded schedules proved independent and order-equivalent are eligible; a sampled crossover is not proof.
observations.identity: Schedule, input, target, compiler, and harness identities are joined for each raw row.

families.falsifier: Use a callback with shared mutation or an injected failure at the lowest index. Any duplicate/missing result, changed failure index, cleanup leak, or speed claim below the gate rejects automatic parallel scheduling.

rule_record.candidate_rule: select bounded parallel scheduling only after legality and D-ACCEL1 cost gate
rule_record.decision: awaiting checker, same-job cost, and owner choice
